close_reason: Fixed in 0d617cd: json_pointer_ext now dispatches through json_pointer_ext_inner with a 32-level MAX_JSON_POINTER_DEPTH cap. Beyond the cap the function returns None (resolution failure) which the dispatcher already handles as a malformed-path error. Two regression tests: deep-path rejection (1000 tokens -> None) and within-cap acceptance (MAX-1 tokens still resolve).
description:
Location: `crate-jmap-server/src/parse.rs:173-222`

  fn json_pointer_ext(value: &Value, path: &str) -> Option<Value> {
      ...
      let (token, remaining) = match after_slash.find('/') { ... };
      if token == "*" {
          ...
          for item in arr {
              match json_pointer_ext(item, remaining) {       // <-- recursion #1
                  ...
              }
          }
      } else {
          ...
          json_pointer_ext(next, remaining)                  // <-- recursion #2
      }
  }

CONCERN
This is the RFC 8620 §3.7 ResultReference resolver — it walks a client-supplied JSON Pointer path against a previously-parsed JMAP response Value. The recursion is bounded only by the path length and the structure of the Value, both of which originate from the request body.

Two attack inputs both exploit the same primitive:

1. **Deep path**: a request whose ResultReference `path` is, say, `"/a/a/a/..."` repeated 8 KiB deep. `json_pointer_ext` recurses 8192 times — well past Rust's default 2 MiB worker-stack budget (each stack frame is ~50 bytes minimum, so 8192 frames ≈ 400 KiB just for return addresses plus locals; in practice closer to 100-200 frames per stack overflow on a tokio worker).

2. **Wildcard amplification**: a request whose path uses `/*/*/*/*/...` against a Value that is an array-of-arrays of fanout N at each level. Per-call recursion is multiplied by fanout in addition to depth.

Combined with the lack of any explicit depth cap (see sibling bead .89-class on parse_request doc gap), an authenticated client can crash a tokio worker via a single ResultReference call. The dispatcher does not isolate this in a tokio::task::spawn — `json_pointer_ext` runs on the calling worker.

WHAT GOES WRONG
DoS (stack overflow). Crashes the worker thread. Tokio's default panic behavior aborts the whole runtime unless the worker is isolated; even with isolation, the impact is loss-of-service for the in-flight request.

PROPOSED FIX
Two options, in order of preference:

(a) **Iterative rewrite**: convert `json_pointer_ext` from direct recursion to an explicit loop over path tokens with an accumulated Vec. The wildcard branch needs a worklist; the simple-token branch needs no recursion at all. Adds maybe 30 LoC but removes the entire stack-DoS surface.

(b) **Depth cap**: add a max-recursion parameter (e.g. `MAX_POINTER_DEPTH: usize = 32`) and early-return `None` when exceeded. Easier change but is a defense-in-depth Band-Aid; the iterative rewrite is cleaner.

In either case, add a unit test with a 1000-deep path and a 32-fanout 5-deep Value to prove the budget is enforced.

ORACLE
- RFC 6901 (JSON Pointer base spec) and RFC 8620 §3.7 (the `*` wildcard extension) define the grammar but say nothing about depth.
- The serde_json default 128-deep recursion limit applies to parsing the path STRING into the Value, but NOT to `json_pointer_ext` walking it — that walk is library code.

RISK CLASSIFICATION
P2. Authenticated DoS on the dispatcher worker via the canonical JMAP ResultReference path. Affects every deployment built on jmap-server.
title: Security: json_pointer_ext is unbounded recursion over client-supplied path against client-supplied Value (crate-jmap-server/src/parse.rs:173)
